question.problem:
The figure below shows the graph of $f(x).$ Determine $\lim_\limits{x\rightarrow 2} \left(\dfrac{2-7x}{xf(x)+2}\right)^3.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14198442/assets/5059a2cee34ad8547bf1af6239ab4a8356e715cd920707cf5f33d2de105a5c1d.png)
question.worked_solution:
From the graph, we find $\lim_\limits{x\rightarrow 2} f(x)=3.$ Therefore, using the power rule, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to 2}{(\frac{2-7x}{xf(x)+2})}^{3} & ={({lim}_{x\to 2}\frac{2-7x}{xf(x)+2})}^{3} \\  & ={(\frac{2-7(2)}{(2\cdot 3)+2})}^{3} \\  & ={(\frac{-12}{8})}^{3} \\  & ={(\frac{-3}{2})}^{3} \\  & =-\frac{27}{8}.\end{aligned}
$$
